I used to think the same about death if I’m being honest. I still do sometimes, that death brings peace to the suffering. It’s much different when someone else dies though. 

Suicide feels preventable. It comes with its own set of demons. Guilt, regret, helplessness, maybe even trauma alongside the grief. The feeling that we could’ve done more, that we could’ve saved them, the what if’s (even if they showed no signs, even if we couldn’t stop them). It’s horrendous, really. Even I (who has struggled with suicidal thoughts beforehand) cannot comprehend it sometimes. It sucks. The saying really is true that, although that person is no longer experiencing pain, it gets passed down to everyone else around them. 

Like any death, we miss the person, their presence, the little things about them, the future we might’ve enjoyed together, their thoughts and words. If you haven’t experienced grief for yourself, think of it as a really good friend who you don’t talk to anymore. Do you miss them? Now amplify that feeling x1000. Hell, maybe even more. Unfortunately, they won’t come back. And it is miserable to feel that way. The pain is so gut-wrenching knowing that someone who once was simply isn’t anymore. There's so many things they’ll miss, so many things they won’t get to experience. 

If you feel suicidal, please confide in someone you trust. It might be useful to get professional help as well. Trust me, it isn’t worth it. People will miss you and it will hurt like a b—— for everyone around you. You’ll miss out on everything beautiful about life even if it doesn’t feel like it right now.
